requirements.requirement: Create a LUKS-encrypted volume and format it with a filesystem
requirements.summary: A 2GiB backing file was created, cryptsetup luksFormat succeeded (producing a LUKS UUID), the volume was opened as secure_srv and formatted XFS with a valid UUID reported by blkid.
mount -a successfully mounted /dev/mapper/secure_srv at /srv/secure, confirmed by mount output and post-reboot verification.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: crypttab/fstab entries were added with a root-fs-resident keyfile enabling unattended unlock; a full reboot was performed (boot_id changed from fbdf5b2c... to 175dd2d7..., cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots) and post-reboot state shows systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount both active with /srv/secure mounted and pre-reboot test data (baseline.txt) intact, with no manual unlock/mount commands issued after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Data written before reboot survives and remains accessible after reboot
requirements.summary: baseline.txt containing 'baseline-data' was written pre-reboot and read back intact post-reboot from the auto-mounted volume.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: a LUKS2-encrypted volume was created and formatted, mounted at /srv/secure, and configured via crypttab/fstab with a keyfile for unattended unlock. A full node reboot was performed and captured, showing a genuinely changed boot identity (cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), automatic activation of the cryptsetup and mount systemd units with no manual steps, and intact pre-reboot test data afterward. This directly demonstrates the required boot-time behavior rather than relying on configuration alone.
limitations: The keyfile enabling unattended unlock resides on the same unencrypted root filesystem as the LUKS backing file, which is an inherent property of unattended (no external secret store/TPM) auto-unlock rather than a flaw in execution; not treated as a task failure since no such mechanism was specified or available (no spare block device).
A minor leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the reboot mechanism remains on the node; low-risk and not cleaned up, factored into the hygiene score.

The reboot verification covers only a single reboot cycle immediately after configuration; longer-term persistence across multiple reboots was not tested, though this is not part of the stated task contract.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were tightly scoped to the task: package install, backing-file/keyfile creation, LUKS format, filesystem creation, crypttab/fstab configuration, SELinux relabeling, and reboot verification. A temporary test file written to /srv/secure during mount -a verification (cmd-e4ddcd5a762148c6) was promptly removed in the same session (cmd-c858b107ca2743c8), leaving no residue. The reboot itself (cmd-497e459940f74a69) was a necessary, expected part of demonstrating the boot-time requirement and is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. One minor artifact, /tmp/reboot.log (created by the backgrounded systemctl reboot command's output redirection), remains on the node per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; this is low-risk, bounded, and incidental to the reboot mechanism rather than an unnecessary mutation, but is noted as leftover residue. No failed services, no package inconsistency, and no unsafe exposure were introduced (listening-socket and failed-service snapshots are unchanged in kind before/after, differing only by ephemeral PIDs from the reboot).
